title: Adjustment Set Menus across Markov-Equivalent Maximal Ancestral Graphs
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental below field floor: score ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, salvageable=false; validity gate confirmed no bounded same-topic field repair and identified unresolved soundness gaps.
gap_reasons: The attested Theorem 57 concludes inequality of the adjustment and interventional densities, not inequality of their means; the stated Gaussian mean-separation conclusion needs a matching source result or an internal construction.

Its key inference from DAG completeness to beta_Z(Sigma) != beta_Z0(Sigma) silently replaces a density discrepancy by a mean discrepancy; no forbidden-set/open-path case construction discharges that omitted step.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a polynomial-identity route to menu rigidity, a completion-free Gaussian efficiency corollary, and a claimed sharp five-variable boundary; five load-bearing citations were independently recovered and attested from primary sources. The final audit found that DAG density-level adjustment completeness had been used as mean-coefficient separation without a proof, and that the four-node lower-bound enumeration lacked a replayable certified artifact. Closing those defects would establish only the advertised incremental package, not lift it to the field floor.
tldr: One shared valid adjustment set forces two selection-free Markov-equivalent maximal ancestral graphs to have the same complete adjustment menu. Consequently, an adjustable partial ancestral graph has exactly the faithful nonzero-effect Gaussian ordinary-least-squares efficiency problem of any one completion. Runge's corrected known-graph criterion transfers only as a sufficient Gaussian certificate: passing the test certifies a distribution-uniform optimum, whereas failing it is inconclusive on the smaller Gaussian domain. The paper also establishes a sharp five-observed-variable threshold for common nonzero identification without a distribution-uniform optimal adjustment set.
gap: PAG adjustment theory characterizes sets valid throughout a class, but its one-completion enumeration retains a PAG forbidden mask and does not say that any one shared set synchronizes the complete menus of all completions. Known-graph Gaussian efficiency is solved by Runge, yet no verified result transfers the entire feasible optimization problem to an arbitrary PAG completion or gives the sharp full-PAG size of the first nonuniformity obstruction.
fill: Prove the menu-overlap dichotomy using full Gaussian ancestral-model identities and separating witnesses; derive exact completion invariance of feasible sets and variance objectives; and pair an explicit five-node rational witness with a transparent, certifiable four-node lower bound.
